tierNote: The competition is officially the Primera División in every season 1990-91 to 2025-26 (each season row carries tier "Primera División"); "La Liga" is the label the career world uses (CAREER_CLUB_POOL league field). Sponsor names (Liga BBVA, LaLiga Santander, LaLiga EA Sports) were not researched and are not recorded.
method: See _method.md (written by the premier-league shard). La Liga specifics: counted sources are RSSSF (rsssf.org tabless/spanhist8999.html for 1990-91 to 1998-99, spanhist9909.html for 1999-2000, span01.html to span09.html for 2000-01 to 2008-09, span2010.html to span2026.html for 2009-10 to 2025-26) and worldfootball.net (final matchday table, matchday 38, or 42 for the 22-club seasons 1995-96 and 1996-97). ESPN's standings feed is a third agreeing source from 2002-03 on (season=2001 and earlier return no table). RSSSF pages were downloaded with curl and parsed as Latin-1 text. worldfootball.net refuses curl (403) and WebFetch (402) but answers a real browser: its pages were read in a headless Chromium (Playwright) tab on worldfootball.net with a same-origin fetch of each season page, the table parsed from the raw HTML with DOMParser (no summarising), and the rows hand-carried into the ledger input were proven identical by a SHA-256 of each season's rows computed in the browser (36 of 36 match). A season is verified only when every source in its sources list gives the same set of clubs, every count equals the size, and no club appears twice. pos is recorded only when every source prints the same position; otherwise posBySource (same order as sources) and a note.
identityNotes: Real Burgos (RSSSF, the club in the top flight 1990-91 to 1992-93, Real Burgos CF) is printed "Burgos CF" by worldfootball.net; one Burgos club per table, same slot, keyed burgos. canon null.

Merida (1995-96 and 1997-98) is printed "Mérida CP" by RSSSF and "Mérida AD" by worldfootball.net (which files the old CP Mérida under the later club); one Merida club per table, keyed merida. canon null.
Lleida (1993-94) is printed "UE Lleida" by RSSSF and "Lleida CF" by worldfootball.net; keyed lleida. canon null.
Deportivo (canon "Deportivo") is RC Deportivo de La Coruña only. Deportivo Alavés is a different club, keyed alaves, canon "Alaves". ESPN prints the first as "Deportivo" and the second as "Alavés".
Malaga (canon "Malaga") is Málaga CF, in the top flight from 1999-2000. The older CD Málaga (dissolved 1992) is not in any season 1990-91 to 2025-26 here.

Sporting de Gijón (keyed sporting, canon null) is not Sporting CP. Real Sociedad, Real Betis, Real Valladolid, Real Zaragoza, Real Oviedo, Real Murcia, Real Burgos are separate clubs, none merged on "Real".
Atlético Osasuna (RSSSF 1990s) and CA Osasuna are the same club; RCD Español (RSSSF to 1994-95) and RCD Espanyol are the same club.
